items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I made a Beat Meets the Beatles record, and Sebesky writes the charts

ctx.x: Don’t say anything because this might—

I’m swinging. So you know, but now you ran into all the like rock & roll publicists and all that, and the review guys are saying, “oh Pizzarelli has big budget records” and he’s this and he’s that. And like well hey, what am I supposed to do? I’m going to make a small group record? I’m having the time of my life working with the best people, and making good records. And then, there’s the fateful Beatle record. I made a Beat Meets the Beatles record, and Sebesky writes the charts and it’s killing and there’s…

items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And Sebesky was a big part of my life in the ‘90s and well just from the ‘90s all the way ‘til his passing.

ctx.x: And so you know that kind of thing, but I mean the good news is is there’s a lot of great music out there. There’s a lot of kids who now can learn in high school and in college from real live great teachers of jazz. I mean a guy like Isaiah, they — you know Isaiah and Mike, and Mike’s a product of the New School I think, too. And Isaiah out of Juilliard. And they’ll sit and they’ll sing choruses on these records they listen to. I make it sound like these records they listen to — but they’re so immersed in it. And…

mentioned that Sebesky record a number of times in other interviews I was looking at today. And Sebesky was a big part of my life in the ‘90s and well just from the ‘90s all the way ‘til his passing. You know somebody like Don Sebesky, you know, writing these arrangements and then you start to see how he harmonizes stuff and you go oh yeah that was cool. So when you start to write the chords out for somebody you go what would Don have done here? You know that was a gift.

Yeah that “Time and Love” song, it took me a long time to realize besides using the melody from the Bach, he pretty much used the chart. He used Bach’s chords and wrote that beautiful thing. It just — every time it really gets to me.
